learn: How the first-half topics connect into one pipeline
Self-attention and the Transformer, recomputed by hand
Decoding, KV cache and serving trade-offs
Fine-tuning methods, plus a mixed set of practice calculations
intro.why: A consolidation point: the formulas and trade-offs of M2–M7 reappear together in design questions, and the second half (alignment, prompting, retrieval, agents, evaluation, safety) builds on them.

sections.title: The first-half arc
sections.plain: One story: train a model on lots of text, build it efficiently, generate from it, serve it cheaply, and specialise it.
sections.body:
The first half follows a single model through its life:

  1. Pre-training (M2): next-token prediction on cleaned, deduplicated, tokenized web-scale text, sized by scaling laws.
  2. Architecture (M3): the modern Transformer block (pre-norm RMSNorm, RoPE, SwiGLU, MoE).
  3. Training efficiency (M4): memory accounting, mixed precision, FlashAttention, long context.
  4. Decoding (M5): prefill/decode, sampling rules, KV cache.
  5. Serving (M6): compression, speculative decoding, batching, paging, cost.
  6. Fine-tuning (M7): SFT, instruction tuning, PEFT, merging, distillation.

Recurring theme: memory and memory traffic, not raw arithmetic, are the usual bottleneck, in training (optimizer states, activations, attention matrix) and in serving (weights and KV cache read every step).

sections.title: Transformer and attention recap
sections.plain: Each token asks a question (query), compares it with every token's label (key), and collects a weighted mix of their contents (values).
sections.body:
$$\text{Attention}(Q,K,V)=\text{softmax}\Big(\frac{QK^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} + M\Big)V$$

M is the causal mask (−∞ above the diagonal) so a decoder cannot look ahead. Multi-head attention runs several of these in parallel on different projections; each block adds a feed-forward network, residual connections and normalisation.

Worked (ex1): Q = [(1,0), (0,1), (1,1)], K = [(1,0), (1,1), (0,1)], V = [(1,2), (0,1), (3,0)], d = 2. Token 1 attends only to itself → output (1, 2). Token 2: scores (0, 0.707) → weights (0.33, 0.67) → (0.33, 1.33). Token 3: scores (0.707, 1.414, 0.707) → (0.248, 0.503, 0.248) → (0.99, 1.00).

Cost: n × n scores per head per layer, so 2000 tokens cost 4× 1000 tokens.

sections.title: Training and scaling recap
sections.plain: Predict the next token on huge clean data; bigger models need proportionally more data.
sections.body:
• Objective: causal language modelling (next token) for generators; masked LM for encoders.
  • Data: filtering, deduplication (exact and near-duplicate), and BPE tokenization; continued pre-training adapts to a domain.
  • Compute: C ≈ 6ND. 70B parameters × 1.4T tokens ≈ 5.9×10²³ FLOPs.
  • Scaling laws: loss falls as a power law in N, D and C. Chinchilla: for fixed compute, scale N and D together, ≈ 20 tokens per parameter; earlier large models were under-trained.

In practice, models meant for heavy use are often trained well past 20 tokens/param, buying cheaper inference with extra training compute.

sections.title: Architecture and efficiency recap
sections.plain: Small changes to the block make training stable and models efficient; memory tricks make training fit.
sections.body:
• Pre-norm + RMSNorm: stable deep training, cheaper normalisation.
  • RoPE: relative position via rotation; extendable context.
  • SwiGLU: gated feed-forward, better at equal size.
  • MoE: top-k of E experts (2/8 = 25% active); memory for all experts; load balancing.
  • Memory: Adam 4 + 4 + 8 = 16 B/param; activations grow with s·b; checkpointing and sharding.
  • Mixed precision: 16-bit compute, fp32 master weights, loss scaling.
  • FlashAttention: exact, tiled, online softmax; Ring Attention distributes long sequences; sparse/linear variants trade accuracy.

sections.title: Serving recap
sections.plain: Generating is limited by reading memory, so shrink what is read and keep the GPU busy.
sections.body:
• Prefill (compute-bound, TTFT) then decode (bandwidth-bound, TPOT).
  • Decoding rules: greedy, beam (B best sequences), top-k, top-p (p = 0.9 on 0.5/0.25/0.15/0.10 keeps 3), temperature.
  • KV cache: 2·L·d·bytes per token (524,288 B for 32 × 4096 × 16-bit; ≈1 GiB per 2048 tokens); GQA/MQA/MLA shrink it.
  • Compression: 1B params fp32 4 GB → int8 1 GB → int4 0.5 GB; pruning.
  • Speculative decoding: (1 − α^(k+1))/(1 − α) tokens per pass, distribution preserved.
  • Systems: continuous batching, chunked prefill, paged attention; cost per million = price ÷ tokens ($2/h at 100 tok/s ≈ $5.56).

sections.title: Fine-tuning recap and mixed practice
sections.plain: Specialise with SFT and LoRA, protect old skills, and practise the core calculations together.
sections.body:
• SFT with response-only loss; instruction tuning across many tasks for zero-shot instruction following.
  • PEFT: prompt/prefix tuning, adapters, LoRA (r(d + k) parameters; r = 8 on 1000² = 1.6%), QLoRA (4-bit base).
  • Merging (task vectors) and distillation (soft targets at temperature T).
  • Catastrophic forgetting: replay, PEFT, regularisation, broad evaluation.

Mixed practice: (1) 7B × 140B tokens → 5.9×10²¹ FLOPs. (2) 3B full fine-tuning → 48 GB. (3) 8k vs 2k context → 16× attention work. (4) top-p 0.8 on 0.5/0.25/0.15/0.10 → 3 tokens. (5) GQA-8 cache at 4096 tokens → 512 MiB. (6) LoRA r = 16 on 4096² → 131,072 parameters (0.78%).

sections.title: Further insights and misconceptions
sections.body:
• Design questions usually combine two topics: e.g. "fit a 13B model for 32k-context chat on one GPU" needs quantization, GQA and paged KV.
  • Units trip people up: GB (10⁹) vs GiB (2³⁰); bits vs bytes; parameters vs tokens.
  • Exact vs approximate: FlashAttention, speculative decoding and paged attention change speed, not outputs; quantization, pruning and sparse attention can change outputs.

code.title: Attention by hand with a causal mask
code.explain: Computes QKᵀ/√d for three tokens, applies a causal mask and softmax (rows (1, 0, 0), (0.33, 0.67, 0), (0.248, 0.503, 0.248)), mixes the values, and prints how score entries grow 4× and 16× as n doubles and quadruples.
mistakes: Masking after softmax instead of before.
code.code:
"""Scaled dot-product attention by hand, with a causal mask, and the quadratic cost of context."""
import numpy as np
np.set_printoptions(precision=3, suppress=True)
Q = np.array([[1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0], [1.0, 1.0]])
K = np.array([[1.0, 0.0], [1.0, 1.0], [0.0, 1.0]])
V = np.array([[1.0, 2.0], [0.0, 1.0], [3.0, 0.0]])
d = Q.shape[1]
S = Q @ K.T / np.sqrt(d)
print("scores QK^T / sqrt(d):\n", S)
mask = np.triu(np.ones_like(S), 1).astype(bool)
S_causal = np.where(mask, -np.inf, S)
P = np.exp(S_causal - S_causal.max(1, keepdims=True)); P /= P.sum(1, keepdims=True)
print("causal attention weights (each row sums to 1, no peeking ahead):\n", P)
print("output = weights @ V:\n", P @ V)
for n in (1000, 2000, 4000):
    print(f"n = {n}: score entries {n*n:,} ({(n/1000)**2:.0f}x the n=1000 cost)")

code.title: First-half formula sheet
code.explain: Recomputes one headline number per formula: 6ND (5.9×10²³), MoE 25% active, Adam 16 GB per billion parameters, attention 4×, top-p keeps 3, KV 524,288 B/token, quantized sizes, $5.56 per million tokens, and LoRA 1.6%.
code.code:
"""First-half formula sheet: one worked number for each core formula."""
N, D = 70e9, 1.4e12
print(f"training compute C = 6ND = 6 x {N:.0e} x {D:.1e} = {6*N*D:.2e} FLOPs; tokens per parameter {D/N:.0f}")
print(f"MoE top-2 of 8 experts: {2/8:.0%} of expert weights active per token")
print(f"Adam training bill: 4 + 4 + 8 = 16 B/param -> 1B params = {16*1e9/1e9:.0f} GB before activations")
print(f"attention cost ratio n=2000 vs n=1000: {(2000/1000)**2:.0f}x")
p = [0.5, 0.25, 0.15, 0.10]; c = 0; kept = 0
for x in p:
    if c >= 0.9 - 1e-9: break
    c += x; kept += 1
print(f"top-p 0.9 on {p}: keeps {kept} tokens")
kv = 2 * 32 * 4096 * 2
print(f"KV cache: 2 x 32 x 4096 x 2 = {kv:,} B/token; 2048 tokens = {kv*2048/2**30:.1f} GiB")
print(f"weights: 1B params fp32 {4:.1f} GB -> int8 {1:.1f} GB -> int4 {0.5:.1f} GB")
tph = 100 * 3600
print(f"cost: $2/h at 100 tok/s = {tph:,} tok/h -> ${2/tph*1e6:.2f} per million tokens")
print(f"LoRA r=8 on 1000x1000: {8*(1000+1000):,} params = {8*2000/1e6:.1%} of the matrix")
